model.name: Content Publication
model.purpose: Represent one governed content-publication operation that binds an external content revision, records review and authority, issues a release instruction, observes origin and downstream delivery, and preserves corrections or removal without absorbing the systems it coordinates.
model.scope_statement: Owns publication-case identity and lineage, target bindings and release metadata snapshots, editorial workflow, review and clearance assertions, decisions, immutable release instructions, packages, channel bindings, delivery attempts, discovery and syndication projections, availability observations, correction, update, retraction, withdrawal and takedown events, provenance, access, retention and interoperability. Content, Publication or Edition, actor, channel, rights, rendition, communication, analytics and record masters remain external.
in_scope: Publication-case identity, authority, target revision bindings, metadata snapshot, workflow, review, clearances and decision evidence
Release instructions, packages, representations, channels, delivery, canonical locations, discovery, feeds, subscriptions and verified availability
Post-publication observation, correction, retraction, withdrawal, takedown, lifecycle, provenance, retention, interoperability and safe agents
out_of_scope: Independent content, edition, actor, organization, role, platform, channel, rights, licence, translation, rendition, communication, analytics or record master lifecycles
Treating approval as availability, delivery acknowledgement as audience reach, syndication as origin authority, unpublishing as erasure or a representation as an edition
Operating publishing platforms, determining legal rights, guaranteeing indexing or reach, moderating all audience interaction or deleting referenced masters

boundary_notes.distinction: The external edition master owns bibliographic identity and edition lineage; this aggregate owns a governed operation that may publish a referenced edition. The registry parent is not an approved relation row.
Those masters own authored meaning and revision history. This model binds the exact revision and records whether, where and under whose authority it was released.
External masters own endpoint, platform and media identities. This case stores release-specific bindings, attempts and observations without copying their inventories.
Their masters own normative rules. This model records scoped clearance assertions and evidence for one release decision.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Communication, Notification, Analytics, Audit and Record
boundary_notes.distinction: Those systems own messages, measurements and records; this case binds qualified references needed to explain publication outcomes.

owner_package_requirements: Content, edition, organization, person, role, channel, platform, rights, licence, communication, analytics, record and policy registries
Master mappings for content, editions, revisions, renditions, translations, actors, channels, endpoints and rights
Editorial, release, correction, access, privacy, retention and agent policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint publication-case, release-instruction, delivery, observation, change-notice and lifecycle-event IDs; preserve every external master identifier.

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by authoritative master-system publication-case identifier, scope profile and lineage head, never title, URL, date or digest.
Keep content revision, edition, representation, instruction, delivery, observed availability and correction state distinct.
patch_rules: Extensions declare scope, authority, rights, lifecycle, access and interoperability effects.
Released instructions, decisions, delivery evidence and change notices are immutable; corrections create successors.
Never silently change target revision, authority, embargo, canonical location, rights, observed result or retention.
compatibility_rules: Ignore additive fields only when identity, boundary, authority, content binding, lifecycle, evidence and provenance survive.
Protocol projections pin versions and declare information loss.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system publication-case identifier qualified by source and profile.
Dimension UUID when neither preceding identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; separate scheduled, effective, decision, release, delivery, observation, change, ingestion and knowledge times.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, case and release binding, source versions, actor, event and knowledge times, access marking and provenance.

policies: The publication case is not a Content, Creative Work, Document, Publication, Edition, Person, Organization, Role, Channel, Platform, Rights, Licence, Translation, Rendition, Dataset, Communication, Analytics, Audit or Record master.
Draft, approval, release instruction, origin delivery, downstream propagation, availability observation and change notice remain separate.
Publication ownership never transfers or cascades ownership of referenced masters.
Agents cannot publish, disclose protected content, waive rights, retract, take down or dispose records without delegated authority.

read: Resolve access purpose, case profile, policies, target bindings, decisions, instructions, deliveries, observations, changes, exceptions and holds.
create: Bind stable case identity, boundary, owner, mandate, profile and authoritative master mappings before review or release.
update: Append successor decisions, instructions, delivery attempts, observations, notices and lifecycle events with authority, reason, event time, knowledge time and expected revision.
delete: Apply publication, privacy, legal-hold and records retention policy; retire or tombstone the case separately and never cascade deletion to external masters.

responsibilities: Own purpose, scope, mandate and lifecycle.

responsibilities: Own intake, review stages, metadata and decision evidence.

roles.name: Rights and policy steward
responsibilities: Own licence, privacy, embargo and legal clearance assertions.

roles.name: Accessibility and quality reviewer
responsibilities: Own test methods, findings, exceptions and conformance evidence.

roles.name: Release manager
responsibilities: Own immutable instructions, packages, schedules and rollback controls.

roles.name: Channel and distribution steward
responsibilities: Own endpoint bindings, delivery attempts and propagation checks.

roles.name: Correction and takedown authority
responsibilities: Authorize successor notices and preservation behavior.

roles.name: Records and security steward
responsibilities: Own protected views, holds, retention, disclosure and auditability.

access.default_rule: Deny embargoed content, personal data, confidential drafts, credentials, unpublished endpoints, legal review and restricted analytics unless a purpose-bound policy permits the minimum necessary view.
exceptions: Declared publisher, regulator, auditor, emergency, court or rights-holder access must cite authority, be time-limited, scoped and logged.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, publication case, operation, authority, policy, RFC 3339 time, affected fields, source revision and outcome without unnecessary protected content.

read_order: Read Dimension publication, content, rights, privacy, security, records and agent policies.
Read this model and linked content, edition, actor, channel, policy, communication, analytics and audit models before mutation.

coverage.claim: Covers one governed content-publication case from intake and review through instruction, distribution, observation, correction and disposition.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok each timed out on one bounded attempt; no independent external result was admitted.
The Publication / Edition parent is candidate registry metadata, not an approved relation edge.
Platform-specific APIs, newsroom standards, scholarly publishing rules, app-store workflows and jurisdictional notice duties require separate profiles.
Sitemaps describe discovery hints and do not prove crawling, indexing, ranking or public reach.
conflicts: Editorial approval, rights clearance, release instruction, successful delivery and public availability are not interchangeable.
A content resource, edition, revision, representation, rendition, canonical URI and delivery URL can overlap but retain different identity and lifecycle rules.
Correction, update, retraction, withdrawal, takedown, unpublish, tombstone and erasure have different authority and preservation effects.
regional_assumptions: Copyright, privacy, accessibility, retention and takedown duties depend on jurisdiction, audience and channel.
Platform acceptance and HTTP success do not establish legal publication or audience receipt.
Required notices, preservation periods and correction practices vary by sector.
adversarial_checks: Reject a case without stable identity, target revision, owner, mandate, profile and lineage head.
Reject approval represented as public availability, an HTTP acknowledgement represented as audience reach, or syndication represented as authoritative origin publication.
Reject silent overwrite of decisions, instructions, evidence, corrections or retractions.
Reject autonomous publication, protected disclosure, rights waiver, takedown or disposal outside delegated authority.
Reject timestamps without seconds and an explicit RFC 3339 offset.
